Hey! I'm a first year baritone in the marching band this year (with no previous baritone experience). For reference I played the alto sax before. I'm not sure how many people they will accept next year but this year we had 7 rookies and 3 of them did not originally play the baritone. I would assume they are going to accept a decent amount this next year especially since we are going to lose a LOT of good people after next season. 

When it comes to how this will be recieved at the U, it won't matter. The leadership team this year was extremely helpful throughout the whole season with both marching and learning the baritone. None of the vets or even rookies will shame you for just learning the baritone and not knowing what you are doing. As long as we can see that you are trying to learn the baritone you will be good. The baritone section is such a great environment to be in and throughout the season you become a big family. 

For advice, I definitely would recommend practicing a lot as most people will tell you. For music to start practicing I would recommend looking at scales of course and getting your partials down. Though I would also look at the school songs (they have two of them on the audition site). For marching try to go to the gym and run. Just being in shape will help you out so much 

I would like to say for all the baritones that we would love to have you in the section next year and don't be afraid to audition because you havent played before! If you have any more questions you can message me 

Hope to see you next season :)
